patterns.key_values: custom borderless break-reminder HUD over the live desktop; wide (~520-560pt) translucent wallpaper-tinting glass card, radius ~24-32pt; layout = leading timer-icon + [primary value (countdown) over secondary reassurance copy], then a full-width action row; one prominent luminance-filled primary + N quiet outlined snooze pills; no traffic lights (correct for an overlay, like a sheet/alert)
break-reminder / health-nudge overlay: countdown (00:40) + graduated deferral (Start break now / +1m / +5m / +15m) — choice-architecture snooze ladder as the core interaction
UNSEEN but near-certain — LookAway is a menu-bar-resident break utility; the HUD is its interruption surface. Recorded as a knowledge gap, not evidence

signature_moves: Signals the primary action by LUMINANCE, not the system accent hue: because the whole panel is a wallpaper-tinted warm glass, a blue controlAccentColor would clash — so 'Start break now' is promoted with a brighter frosted fill while the snooze options recede to translucent outlined pills. Correct action hierarchy achieved without the user's accent (Von Restorff via brightness).

Emotional de-escalation of an unwelcome interruption: a break nag is inherently hostile, so LookAway wraps it in warmth — soft rounded-terminal type, a calm sleepy-eyes mascot, warm amber body copy that reassures rather than commands ('Your eyes will appreciate this'), and a wallpaper-adaptive glass that feels part of the desktop rather than an alien alert. The aesthetic IS the compliance strategy.

Graduated snooze ladder (+1m / +5m / +15m) beside the primary — structured, low-friction deferral instead of a binary dismiss; keeps the choice count at 4 (Hick's) while giving the user agency over the interruption.
defects: UI Contrast Dilution (#10, borderline) — the outlined snooze pills' translucent-cream stroke on dark maroon likely falls under the 3:1 non-text floor; the borders barely read. Corrective: raise stroke contrast or give the recessive pills a faint translucent fill for a firmer edge.

Accent binding absent (no controlAccentColor) — a native reading would bind selection/primary to the user's accent; here it's luminance-only. Systematic + purposeful + accessible on a warm-tinted HUD, so recorded as a SIGNATURE per defect-vs-signature, not an anti-pattern — but it is the one place a strict native reading diverges, and it means the surface is EXCLUDED from macOS accent canon.

Evidence poverty (not a design defect): one surface (the pre-break HUD), one state, from a stylized marketing render over a single warm wallpaper. Unseen: the menu-bar extra, settings, onboarding, the full-screen break overlay itself, and glass-tint robustness on a cool/dark desktop. All metrics are ratio estimates at ~@2x.

aesthetic.direction: warm wellness / calm-nudge — a friendly consumer register outside the range-map families: rounded-terminal sans + warm magenta→peach gradient palette + wallpaper-adaptive glass + a resting-face mascot. Deliberately soft, the opposite of a pro-tool's neutral density.

psychology: Aesthetic-usability effect (Kurosu & Kashimura) — THE core mechanism: an interruption is inherently unwelcome, so the polished warm glass + mascot + gentle copy buy goodwill that makes users comply with the break rather than disable the app. Polish here is a retention lever, not decoration.
Von Restorff / action singularity — one bright luminance-filled primary among quiet outlined secondaries makes the intended action ('Start break now') pop pre-attentively, even without an accent hue.
Hick's Law — exactly 4 options at the decision point (start + three snoozes); minimal decision cost during a glanceable interruption.

Choice architecture / forgiveness (Thaler & Sunstein; Lidwell) — the graduated snooze ladder gives structured deferral instead of an all-or-nothing dismiss; the interruption tolerates 'not now' without losing the reminder.
Fitts's Law — large ~40pt-tall capsule targets on a full-screen overlay; easy to acquire from anywhere on screen.
notes: The ONLY app UI is the floating panel inside cover.png (2400x1260) — a stylized product render, not a captured screenshot, so scale is semi-knowable and every metric is a ~@2x ratio estimate at medium-low confidence. The panel is genuinely translucent (wallpaper diagonal bands visible through it) and warm-tints to the desktop = Liquid-Glass-era adaptive material — but the surface is fully custom (no native chrome), so lineage is inferred NATIVE from category + material behavior rather than confirmed from native tells. Everything outside/around the panel — the near-black warm-olive backdrop, the 'Smart breaks...' bold rounded headline, and the sleepy-eyes app icon (a resting calm face, magenta→peach gradient on a black squircle with a warm Liquid-Glass top rim-light) — is BRAND evidence, analyzed but never conflated with app-UI tokens.
